text:
Comparing the file against `ms` at tag 2.1.3, everything matches except one line in the `parse()` switch statement. The years branch reads:

```javascript
case 'years':
case 'year':
case 'yrs':
case 'yr':
case 'y':
  return n / y;
```

The upstream 2.1.3 code returns `n * y` here, not `n / y`. Since `y = d * 365.25 = 31557600000`, the patched build turns `ms('1y')` into `1 / 31557600000 ≈ 3.17e-11` instead of `31557600000`. This is a real, caller-observable defect (any config string like `'2 years'` silently produces a near-zero duration), and the bundled test suite evidently has no coverage for parsing year units, so it stays green.

A test asserting the correct behaviour fails immediately on the patched build:

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "proof-test.js", "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar ms = require('./');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('fails on the patched build', function () {\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1y'), 31557600000, 'ms(\"1y\") should be 1 year in milliseconds');\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('2yrs'), 2 * 31557600000, 'ms(\"2yrs\") should be 2 years in milliseconds');\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('-1y'), -31557600000, 'ms(\"-1y\") should be -1 year in milliseconds');\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "The years case in parse() uses `return n / y;` instead of `n * y`, so year-unit strings like '1y' parse to ~3.17e-11 ms instead of 31557600000 ms. The rest of the file matches ms 2.1.3."}
```
